propositions: A deterministic offline AST gate must detect when modules outside approved composition roots or provider-credential boundaries perform prohibited ambient config/env reads, credential reads, or provider backend access.

The gate must reuse gen_env_registry's env-read detection machinery (scan, KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS matchers, _is_os_environ, _str_literal) as a single source and add new logic for callee/receiver aliasing resolution and category 3/4/6 rules.
Unresolved env reads (shim-shaped callee absent from KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS table, or dynamic env-name argument) must fail closed and be reported as unresolved-env-read violations.

The approved-seam registry and owner sets must be derived at runtime from existing registries (_child_env.owned_secret_names, @register decorator scan, gen_env_registry.scan + _deprecations.REGISTRY) rather than hand-copied, and a newly declared env name/credential lacking an owner must fail.

Receiver-object aliasing (e.g., src = os.environ; src.get('SECRET')) and callee aliasing (import as, from import, local bind) must be resolved to canonical forms so all access patterns are classified uniformly.

An initial legacy-exception set (exact path+symbol+rationale entries, no globs or directories) enumerates current below-seam reads to allow the gate to pass the current tree; C3 drains this set to empty.
